claims.title: Fixed-budget public randomness realizes exactly the dyadic codebook mixtures, and the shared-randomness value is reached with finitely many fair bits iff some optimal mixture is dyadic
claims.scope: any finite rational game of scenario rows against deterministic zero-error codebook columns, with b independent fair public bits
assumptions: the seed is public to encoder and all decoders and is drawn before the source state
the scenario is chosen obliviously to the realized seed
the fixed-budget controller selects a codebook as a deterministic function of the b bits
nonclaims: elementary: k-uniform approximation of optimal strategies is classical (Althofer 1994; Lipton-Young 1994), and that bounded-depth fair-coin samplers realize exactly the dyadic laws is the Knuth-Yao (1976) observation; only the exact dyadic dichotomy statement for these games is claimed
fair independent bits are assumed rather than extracted from a physical source
a seed-observing adversary is not covered

claims.title: Two-sided Theta(2^-b) gap for non-dyadic shared-randomness optima without nondegeneracy assumptions: 2^-b/(D_A q) <= V_b - V* <= Delta_S floor(s/2) 2^-b
claims.scope: finite rational games whose optimal mixture set contains no dyadic point, for every bit budget b
assumptions: the seed is public to encoder and all decoders and is drawn before the source state
the scenario is chosen obliviously to the realized seed
payoff entries are rational with common denominator D_A and the value is p/q in lowest terms
s is the support size of any optimal mixture and Delta_S is the largest row range over that support; a basic optimal mixture with s <= min(R, n) exists by Shapley-Snow
nonclaims: the upper constant Delta_S floor(s/2) is not claimed tight; only the lower constant is shown attained (K3 and ST-M27 at radius 1/2, even b)
the rounding is Hamilton (largest-remainder) apportionment; the Lipton-Young k-uniform rate is complementary (worse in b, independent of s and n)
nothing is claimed for irrational payoff matrices

claims.title: Price of the shared-randomness value: the least expected number of fair bits that attains V* is the minimum over the optimal set of the Knuth-Yao cost (attained), and no bounded-bit sampler attains a non-dyadic optimum
claims.scope: finite rational shared-codebook games and exact samplers driven by a stopping time on i.i.d. fair public bits
assumptions: the seed is public to encoder and all decoders and is drawn before the source state
the scenario is chosen obliviously to the realized seed
the sampler must induce an optimal codebook law exactly
Knuth-Yao (1976) optimality of DDG sampling (tail bound, cost formula, H + 2 bound) is used as a cited standard result
nonclaims: the tail optimality, the DDG cost formula and the H + 2 bound are Knuth-Yao 1976, reproved for completeness and not new; only the composition with the optimal set is claimed
the minimum over a non-singleton optimal set is attained but not computed in general
the H + 2 upper bound is cited and numerically checked rather than reproved

claims.title: t uniform L-ary public tosses (L >= 2) attain the shared-randomness value iff the optimal set meets L^-t Z^n, with gap at least 1/(D_A q L^t) otherwise
claims.scope: finite rational shared-codebook games with t uniform L-ary public tosses
assumptions: the seed is public to encoder and all decoders and is drawn before the source state
the scenario is chosen obliviously to the realized seed
payoff entries are rational with common denominator D_A and the value is p/q in lowest terms
uniform independent L-ary tosses with L >= 2
the controller selects a codebook as a deterministic function of the tosses
nonclaims: building a uniform L-ary coin from fair bits is itself priced by ST-T312 and is not free
for L = 1 the ring decision is made only for single points

claims.title: Exact b-bit K3 value curve V_b = 2 - floor(2^b/3)/2^b never reaches five thirds
claims.scope: the K3 public-randomness game with three point-mass models and complete prefix length permutations of (1,2,2)
assumptions: b independent fair public bits
the model is chosen obliviously to the seed
nonclaims: the one-third coordination value of ST-M47 is realized only in the limit of unbounded bits
not claimed for games other than K3, ST-M26, ST-M45 and ST-M27 at radius 1/2

claims.title: Skew K3 shared-TV game at radius one half has b-bit gap exactly one tenth of the K3 gap
claims.scope: K3 with nominal prior (4/5,1/10,1/10) at TV radius 1/2 under shared-randomness expected prefix coding
assumptions: the five-vertex by three-codebook matrix certified by the repository solver (columns give the short codeword to states 1, 0, 2)
b independent fair public bits and a seed-oblivious TV adversary
nonclaims: the one-tenth ratio is specific to this radius and prior

claims.title: Exact K3 coordination costs eight thirds expected fair bits while ST-M21 costs exactly one bit and ST-M27 at radius at most 7/15 costs none
claims.scope: K3, ST-M26, ST-M45 and ST-M27 at radius 1/2 (singleton uniform optimum); ST-M21 and the K4 nonoracle example (singleton half-half optimum); ST-M27 at radii 2/5 and 7/15 (optimal set contains a pure law; a segment at 7/15), and every radius k/30 <= 7/15
assumptions: the optimal set is the singleton uniform law, the singleton (1/2,1/2) law, or contains a pure law, as certified by optimal-set vertex enumeration in the reduced game
fair public bits and seed-oblivious adversaries
nonclaims: the 8/3-bit cost of an exact uniform ternary choice is classical (Knuth-Yao 1976; Lumbroso 2013); the model result is its identification as the exact coordination price of these games
the decision gain priced here is coordination randomness, not evidence about a simulator

claims.title: One uniform L-ary public toss attains the K3 shared-randomness value iff three divides L (also for ST-M27 at radius 1/2); for ST-M21 and K4 iff two divides L
claims.scope: K3 and ST-M27 at radius 1/2 for L = 1..12; K3 for all L^t <= 1000 with 3 not dividing L; ST-M21 and K4 for L <= 12
assumptions: uniform independent L-ary tosses
the controller selects a codebook as a deterministic function of the tosses
nonclaims: the statements are for the listed instances; the general criterion is ST-T313

claims.title: Exact finite certification of the random-bit price on committed and seeded random instances
claims.scope: K3 for b <= 12; eight committed matrices for b <= 10; 300 seeded random integer games for b <= 6; 200 seeded random rational laws for the Knuth-Yao identities; L <= 12 coin alphabets; repository cross-check of seven matrices plus the ST-M45 value; ST-M27 radius sweep
assumptions: exact Fraction arithmetic except the floating-point entropy sandwich
repository matrices are cross-checked against the committed exact solvers
nonclaims: the bounded enumeration is not by itself a proof for all b; the proofs are in the derivation
for ST-M45 only the value, not the matrix, is matched against the repository
